skills.description: Patterns and timed problem solving aligned to Google phone and onsite coding rounds.
skills.target: 145 curated problems across 24 weeks with Saturday retention tests.

modules.title: Foundations: arrays, hashing, two pointers
modules.overview: Build automatic recognition for linear scans, hash maps, and sorted two-pointer moves—the highest-frequency phone screen building blocks.
modules.whyGoogle: Most Google screens start medium-easy on arrays/strings; speed and clean invariants here save onsite energy.
learnItems: Hash map complement and frequency templates
Two pointers on sorted arrays and palindromes
Sliding window distinct vs at-most-K variants
When to sort vs when hashing wins
checklist: Solve Two Sum and 3Sum without hints
Explain duplicate handling in 3Sum
Code longest substring without repeating chars in one pass
State complexities before coding on a new problem
modules.youtubeSearch: NeetCode arrays hashing two pointers playlist

modules.title: Core structures: stacks, heaps, binary search
modules.overview: Monotonic stacks, priority queues, and binary search templates including search on answer for scheduling-style questions.
modules.whyGoogle: Google infra problems often reduce to heaps (top-K) or binary search on monotonic feasibility.
learnItems: Monotonic stack for next greater element
Feasibility check functions for BS on answer
checklist: Implement Koko Eating Bananas from scratch
Solve Meeting Rooms II with heap and explain sweep alternative
Find first/last position in sorted array
Articulate monotonic property before BS on answer

modules.title: Trees, graphs, and topological reasoning
modules.overview: DFS/BFS on trees and graphs, union-find, topo sort, and weighted shortest paths for onsite depth.
modules.whyGoogle: Graph modeling (dependencies, grids, connectivity) is disproportionately common in Google loops.
learnItems: Tree DFS: path, diameter, BST validation
Graph BFS for shortest unweighted paths
checklist: Draw BFS vs DFS choice for Word Ladder
Code Course Schedule II and explain cycle detection
Implement Number of Islands both DFS and BFS
Walk through Network Delay Time priority queue steps

modules.title: DP, greedy proofs, and hard follow-ups
modules.overview: 1D/2D DP, knapsack, LIS, interval greedy, and communicating optimizations under time pressure.
modules.whyGoogle: Onsite rounds extend mediums into DP or greedy proof sketches—partial progress needs clear narration.
checklist: Write edit distance recurrence before table
Solve LIS with patience sorting
Explain why greedy works for non-overlapping intervals
Practice one hard DP (Burst Balloons or Regex) with bounds

skills.description: Language fluency for Google-style backend interviews and clean on-the-fly implementation.
skills.target: Comfort implementing DSA templates in Go with idiomatic slices, maps, and structs.

modules.title: Slices, maps, and runes
modules.overview: Zero-value semantics, append growth, map existence checks, and UTF-8 rune iteration for string problems.
modules.whyGoogle: Interviewers accept Go if you are fluent—awkward slice handling costs credibility.
learnItems: make vs var for slices and maps
Range over string with rune awareness
checklist: Implement two-sum in Go with one pass map
Use sort.Slice for interval problems
Explain slice backing array pitfalls
Run go test on a small table-driven test

modules.title: Interfaces, errors, and testing
modules.overview: Small interfaces, explicit error handling, and table-driven tests mirroring production Go style.
modules.whyGoogle: Design discussions often assume idiomatic error propagation and testability.
learnItems: When to use pointers in receivers
checklist: Write a tiny LRU or min-stack API in Go
Return structured errors for invalid input
Add two table tests including edge cases
Explain nil interface vs typed nil pointer

modules.title: Goroutines, channels, and context
modules.overview: Enough concurrency to discuss worker pools, fan-in/fan-out, and cancellation—not full systems yet.
modules.whyGoogle: Go roles expect sane talk about goroutines even if coding rounds stay sequential.
learnItems: Data race awareness and mutex vs channel
checklist: Sketch parallel URL fetcher with timeout
Explain happens-before for a simple channel
Know when NOT to use goroutines in interviews
Pair with Fundamentals OS threads module

skills.description: OS, memory, and runtime concepts that underpin design and coding follow-ups.
skills.target: Crisp explanations for threads, memory hierarchy, and process lifecycle without buzzwords.

modules.title: Processes, threads, and scheduling
modules.overview: How CPU time is shared, why goroutines map to threads, and where context switches hurt.
modules.whyGoogle: Latency and tail issues often trace back to scheduling and lock contention.
learnItems: Go scheduler M:N model at high level
checklist: Explain why busy-wait is bad
Describe race vs data race
Connect to Go concurrency module
Give one real incident tied to thread pool exhaustion

modules.title: Memory hierarchy and allocation
modules.overview: Stack vs heap, cache locality, and why allocation rate affects GC in Go and JVM languages.
modules.whyGoogle: Performance discussions at Google often mention allocation, caching, and profiling.
learnItems: Big-O vs constant factors at scale
checklist: Explain pointer chasing vs array scan
Relate slice append to realloc
Name one profiling tool you would use
Tie to DSA space complexity answers

skills.description: HTTP, DNS, TCP, and TLS vocabulary for design and reliability conversations.
skills.target: Explain a request path from browser to service with failure modes.

modules.title: DNS, HTTP/2, and REST shape
modules.overview: Resolution chain, connection reuse, status codes, idempotency, and pagination patterns.
modules.whyGoogle: API design rounds assume you know how clients actually reach services.
learnItems: REST idempotency for POST vs PUT
checklist: Walk DNS lookup steps aloud in 2 minutes
Design retry policy for idempotent GET
Explain 502 vs 503 vs 504
Link to Communication module for 6-min recording

modules.title: TCP lifecycle and TLS handshake
modules.overview: Three-way handshake, congestion idea, TLS layers, and where latency hides.
modules.whyGoogle: Global-scale services live or die on connection setup and cross-region RTT.
checklist: Draw TCP handshake
Explain why TLS adds RTTs
Describe SYN flood at high level
Connect to load balancer design week

skills.description: Structured design for L4+ loops: requirements, estimates, data model, and scaling paths.
skills.target: Two full designs per month with written postmortems and trade-off tables.

modules.title: Framing, estimates, and APIs
modules.overview: Repeatable opening: users, QPS, storage, read/write ratio, SLA, and API sketch before boxes.
modules.whyGoogle: Google design interviewers penalize jumping to Kafka without numbers.
learnItems: Read path vs write path separation
checklist: Practice URL shortener estimates in 5 minutes
Write API for create/read/delete
State three non-functional requirements
Time-box yourself to 35 minutes total

modules.title: Storage, indexing, and caching
modules.overview: SQL vs NoSQL choice, sharding keys, replication, cache-aside, and invalidation pitfalls.
modules.whyGoogle: Search, ads, and user data systems all revisit the same storage trade-offs.
learnItems: Primary key and secondary index costs
checklist: Pick sharding key for social feed
Explain cache stampede mitigation
When to introduce CDN vs app cache
Draw read path with cache miss

modules.title: Case studies: feed, search, rate limiter
modules.overview: Apply framing to news feed, typeahead search, and distributed rate limiting.
modules.whyGoogle: These three patterns cover a large fraction of reported Google design prompts.
learnItems: Fan-out on write vs read for feeds
Token bucket vs sliding window log
checklist: Complete one design on whiteboard weekly in weeks 13–20
Document bottlenecks and second-phase scaling
Pair with Mock interview module
Review Google SRE ideas for reliability
modules.youtubeSearch: Google system design news feed rate limiter

skills.description: Think-aloud coding, concise explanations, and behavioral clarity in English.
skills.target: Daily short recordings; every DSA session includes complexity recap aloud.

modules.title: Think-aloud coding
modules.overview: Scripts for clarifying, planning, coding, testing, and follow-ups under interview silence pressure.
modules.whyGoogle: Google hire decisions weight communication as heavily as final code for many levels.
checklist: Record one medium solve with voice only
Cut filler words in second take
Use googleyness englishPractice eng-03 weekly
Peer review one recording

modules.title: STAR and Googleyness delivery
modules.overview: Map stories to rubrics; keep answers under three minutes with measurable results.
modules.whyGoogle: Each onsite interviewer covers different rubrics—story reuse must feel fresh.
checklist: Prepare 10 STAR stories
Practice story-01 and story-03 with timer
List questions for hiring manager
Cross-link googleyness.json prompts

skills.description: Timed cumulative mocks combining coding, light design, and behavioral.
skills.target: Weekly Saturday mocks in latter phases; biweekly before week 17.

modules.title: Timed coding mocks
modules.overview: 45-minute sessions: 5 clarify, 10 plan, 25 code, 5 test—medium/hard from current phase patterns.
modules.whyGoogle: Simulates phone screen pacing and follow-up extensions.
learnItems: Stop and narrate if stuck 3 minutes
Write follow-up idea even if not coded
checklist: Complete 12 timed mocks before week 24
Review recording or scratchpad next day
Track pattern miss rate
Alternate Go and Python if allowed

modules.title: Full loop simulation
modules.overview: Half-day schedule: two coding, one design, one Googleyness—with breaks.
modules.whyGoogle: Build stamina and mental reset between unrelated rounds.
learnItems: Design immediately after coding reset walk
checklist: Run 3 full loops in weeks 21–24
Invite peer or use timer-only
Score using googleyness rubrics
Adjust weak pattern week plan
